faq_plan.q: What is a forklift operator evaluation form?
How do I create a forklift operator evaluation form?

plan.angle: The top 10 is fill-and-sign PDFs and university checklists: an evaluator ticks a sheet once and files it. This page shows the forklift operator evaluation form as a running record: an evaluator scores maneuvers on a tablet in the workplace, a pass writes the certification record with the fields OSHA's rule names, the three-year re-evaluation date is tracked, a near-miss puts the operator back in line for refresher training and a fresh evaluation, and a move to a new truck type opens that truck's own evaluation. The FAQ covers the definition, what OSHA's rule says about timing and the certification record, who can evaluate, and what happens after a failed item.
tab_stories: At Gresford Freight, trainer Tibor Mallinson scores new hire Ebba Coakley on 12 maneuvers on a sit-down counterbalance truck, she passes all 12, and the form writes her certification record with his name as evaluator.

Orrin Bay Foods tracks 38 operators against the three-year evaluation mark; anyone within 60 days of it lands on a due list, and safety manager Gisele Dorsch gets an email naming the 4 operators due this month.

At Strathy Paper, a shift lead logs a near-miss when Zelig Grunwald's forks clip a rack upright; his status changes to refresher due and training lead Fiadh Yeboah gets a Slack direct message to book his refresher and re-evaluation.

Mordaunt Building Supply moves Bartosz Quaid from a sit-down counterbalance truck to the reach truck in the lumber shed; the form opens the reach-truck evaluation, and after he passes, his record lists both truck types.
